metadata.title: Tesla is 'the best choice': Valvetronic Designs founder talks customized vs. everyday cars

content.text:
Austin Huffman, founder of car exhaust system company Valvetronic Designs, sits down with Market Domination host Josh Lipton and Yahoo Finance Senior Autos Reporter Pras Subramanian to discuss the car customization industry and how electric vehicles (EVs) like Tesla (TSLA) come into play.
reviewers who are not familiar, just explain what your company does, what you guys make.
Yeah, absolutely. So, Valvetronic was funded on the principle that people wanted to have the flexibility when they have an exhaust system. So, being able to choose loud and quiet sounds. So, if you start the car in the neighborhood, it's nice and quiet, then when you're on your favorite backroad, you can have it be enjoyable and have that sound when you want to get that audible feedback from your foot pressing the gas, and noise is an important touch point and feedback of
driving. One of the challenges is people don't like Tesla because they feel that the way it accelerates is because it's electric is offputting. It it makes people uh, sick, you know, whatever.
Because they're so used to the the ice, the internal combustion engine cars having that feedback.
So, we always find that although noise is not a people don't think about it as something they would want in their daily car, when you pull the noise away, the car becomes like this quiet isolated box and it forces people to like really sit with their thoughts when everything's so quiet. So the noise is a good distraction.
But there is something so nice about just getting on the the the highway and hearing the exhaust valves click open and it's like this nice roar behind you and then it goes away.
How much of a like a risk if at all would you consider EVs to the business? I I I would imagine some people they must
I have one. I have two actually.
Is that bad news for someone selling exhaust systems?
Not at all. No, so this this is what's fascinating about the EV thing is I have a Tesla Model S Plaid and a Porsche Taycan that we use as film cars and and I use the Tesla as my daily driver. You think I'm this I'm completely it's completely sacrilege.
The Tesla does one thing, the Taycan too. They do something so well, which is just blend into your life. It's like an appliance. But if you're looking for an experience, you're not going to pull an an emotional connection to a Tesla or this electric Porsche. Maybe the Porsche a little bit more. Thing is is those customers who buy our products, they might have an electric vehicle as a daily driver, but they're not modifying that car.
Anybody who buys Teslas, they might modify them a little bit, but they're not our customer in the first place. They're not your off-road Jeep guy wanting an exhaust. They're not going to replace their Porsche GT3 or their fast BMW that has a great sound with a Tesla as an emotional experience. It might be a uh a usability difference, but they're going to look elsewhere for that for that uh enjoyment. They may have a second car or something. So we don't find it's a problem. I actually invite it.
Because it makes everybody else who doesn't like the hobby, they have a great choice. Anytime anybody asks me, what should I buy? What car should I get?
I always say, well what do you want? And they go, I just want something reasonable, comfortable, reliable. And I say go buy a Tesla. I don't want a Tesla. It's the best choice. It's
there's no maintenance, it's simple. I I I think it's a great thing for us. And at the end of the day, people who buy those cars, they're not our customer anyway.
